title: CogniMap3D: Cognitive 3D Mapping and Rapid Retrieval
claim: A video's static scene is isolated via motion cues, matched against persistent memory, updated, and jointly optimized into refined 3D output.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right; colored dashed boxes, memory loop with update/recall arrows
description: A single wide pipeline diagram reads left to right. A vertical film strip of four horse-jumping video frames, with a Time arrow, feeds an orange dashed box holding depth maps and initial camera poses. A downward arrow leads to a Motion Cue row of horse silhouettes, then to an orange Static Scene point cloud. An orange Match arrow goes to a blue stacked Memory Bank block. A blue dashed Recall arrow goes to a Scene in Memory box. Blue dashed Update arrows link the Memory Bank to an Updated Scene point cloud at top center. A curved blue Joint Optimization arrow leads to the large final point cloud with the horse and three refined camera frustums below. Orange marks the current observation and blue marks memory. The eye goes first to the colorful 3D point clouds.
caption: CogniMap3D maintains a cognitive mapping system that recalls, stores, and updates memories. Given an input video, it outputs camera poses and point clouds by isolating static scenes through motion cues, interacting with its memory bank, and optimizing across multiple visits.
abstract: We present CogniMap3D, a bioinspired framework for dynamic 3D scene understanding and reconstruction that emulates human cognitive processes. Our approach maintains a persistent memory bank of static scenes, enabling efficient spatial knowledge storage and rapid retrieval. CogniMap3D integrates three core capabilities: a multi-stage motion cue framework for identifying dynamic objects, a cognitive mapping system for storing, recalling, and updating static scenes across multiple visits, and a factor graph optimization strategy for refining camera poses. Given an image stream, our model identifies dynamic regions through motion cues with depth and camera pose priors, then matches static elements against its memory bank. When revisiting familiar locations, CogniMap3D retrieves stored scenes, relocates cameras, and updates memory with new observations. Evaluations on video depth estimation, camera pose reconstruction, and 3D mapping tasks demonstrate its state-of-the-art performance, while effectively supporting continuous scene understanding across extended sequences and multiple visits.
